_comment: Single source of truth for the landing-page ELEMENT CATALOG + composition (plans/PAGE_COMPOSER.md, Builder Reframe). Read by the Python publisher (domain/composition.py) AND imported by the Vue builder (composables/pageComposer.js). One vocabulary: the canonical key is the section `type` string (no aliases). Each element declares label + ui + kind + channel + heading_role + tokens; the composer uses governed_sections + offer_types (what the page sells) unioned with the packs enabled by goals (why its traffic comes — plans/LANDING_PAGE_GOAL_COMPOSITION.md).
_default_order_comment: default_order is the BASELINE sequence a page gets when the tenant has not dragged anything — plans/BUILDER_SECTION_ORDER.md 4a. It only decides the FREE band; lead/pinned_top/pinned_bottom are fixed by placement regardless. The element run follows the visitor's questions: what is it -> is it any good -> who says so -> tell me more -> who else uses it -> but what about. Trust badges sit beside the price/CTA cluster because trust signals work at the moment of commitment, not a screen earlier. Price/CTA deliberately stay AFTER the persuasion: checkout_cta is non-repeatable, so there is exactly one ask. Per-goal overrides go in goals.<goal>.default_order; none are defined yet, because varying them without evidence would be guessing.
_placement_comment: placement = where a section may sit, and whether the tenant may drag it. lead: bars that legitimately precede the hero (announcement/urgency). pinned_top: the hero block -- NOT movable, because hero_media is the LCP element the renderer emits preload/priority hints for, and one-H1-first is an invariant the semantic outline depends on. free: the tenant orders these. pinned_bottom: always last. none: not a visible section (channel: head). Deliberate divergence from stripe-cart, which let the hero move.
_token_catalog_comment: Powers Advanced Color Settings — the panel is GENERATED from this, grouped by `group`. Keys match theme_tokens (server --sl-<key>, preview --preview-<key>). Adding a token here surfaces it automatically. `kind:gradient` pairs cta_from/cta_to.

lead_capture._comment: Squeeze page. checkout_cta IS the inline form -- removing it would remove the thing the page exists for. hero_media is optional and doubles as a background image; a capture page works with no image at all. Covers capture_email, capture_phone and capture_email_phone: the field differs, the page does not.

lead_call._comment: Click-to-call. The local-business shape: hours, address and NAP ARE the persuasion, so seller_profile (ungoverned, so simply addable) earns its place here more than on any other lead page. A hero is genuinely optional -- a phone number above the fold beats a photograph. trust_badges ADDED 2026-09-16 (author): a click-to-call page is the one lead shape where the visitor is about to phone a stranger about something urgent, and nothing on the page has reassured them yet -- there is no price, no checkout and no cart to do it. Badges are the only slot for licensed / insured / 24-hour, which is exactly what that decision turns on.

lead_bridge._comment: The thinnest page here: one headline, one outbound button. ALWAYS noindex,nofollow -- see plans/LEAD_GEN_PAGES.md 5. trust_badges ADDED 2026-09-16 (author): a bridge page asks the visitor to leave for somewhere else, and has no commerce furniture of its own to earn that. hero_media ADDED 2026-09-16, REVERSING "No hero_media: a bridge page that loads a hero image is a slower bridge" (author, seeing a real advertorial: "Hero-less page works but doesn't look as good"). The speed argument was sound and lost to a stronger one -- a bridge page that looks unfinished does not get the click it was optimised to deliver quickly. Tenants who want the faster page can still switch the section off per page.

lead_social._comment: Link-in-bio. The ONLY lead shape with no checkout_cta: its CARDS are the calls to action, and a stray 'Learn More' button pointing at one profile is the bug this composition exists to fix. No `hero` either -- the identity header (avatar + brand + links) does that job, and an offer headline repeated above a link hub is noise. social_links, link_cards and catalog_grid are ungoverned, so the tenant adds them and they render. EXCLUDES WIDENED 2026-09-13 (author): a link hub is an identity page and a list of destinations, so the persuasion furniture of a sales page -- testimonials, ratings, client logos, FAQ, before/after, quotes, content blocks -- has nothing to persuade anyone of here. The name and slogan under the avatar cover the one line of prose these pages actually want. Everything named here was ALREADY unreachable at render; the problem was that the builder went on offering it.

tip_jar._comment: A tip jar. Transactional, so it keeps the price selector and the CTA -- but it is not a SALES page: nothing ships, nothing is delivered, and there is no purchase decision to de-risk, so the trust badges a checkout page leans on ('Secure checkout', 'Money-back guarantee') have nothing to say here and are excluded outright, as on a link hub (author, 2026-09-13). The tip_jar ELEMENT is excluded for the same reason `single` excludes it: a page that already takes tips does not link to another one. The refund policy stays -- see plans/PAY_WHAT_YOU_WANT.md 5f, which is an open question rather than a settled one. The CTA says "Send tip", not "Buy Now": nothing is being bought, and the verb on the button is the last thing a supporter reads before their card is charged.

_goal_comment: Second composition axis: the tenant's GOAL / traffic source (plans/LANDING_PAGE_GOAL_COMPOSITION.md). A goal enables capability PACKS on top of the offer_type base — never a hand-maintained offer_type x goal matrix. Packs are union-only: they add, never remove, so a page with no goal composes exactly as it did before goals existed (no migration). A pack has two halves because the two kinds of section behave differently. `seeds` are content-bearing body elements (faq, testimonials, ...) that render nothing until a tenant fills them in — the create wizard seeds them as empty scaffolds into builder state and they are tenant-owned from then on, so changing goal never deletes copy. `sections` are governed sections the goal turns on; that suits DERIVED head/sidecar output (structured_data, llms_txt) needing no tenant input, and is empty until those exist (Phase 3) — the mechanism is here so they slot in without a renderer change. Editing guide: docs/CONFIGURING_GOALS.md. NEVER delete or rename a goal — pages that stored it would stop validating and could no longer be saved or re-rendered. Retire one with "deprecated": true, which hides it from the wizard while existing pages keep validating and composing.

paid_ads.label: Paid ads
paid_ads.note: Ad traffic converts fast or bounces. Adds a benefits block and an FAQ so the page answers the ad's promise and the obvious objections.

search_seo.label: Search-friendly
search_seo.note: Adds search-friendly content: an FAQ, plus (later) structured data and llms.txt from the offer.

social.label: Social
social.note: Built to convert a scrolling audience: adds social proof — testimonials, rating, client logos.

email_list.label: Email list
email_list.note: A warm audience that already knows you. Adds nothing extra — straight to the offer.

minimal.label: Minimal
minimal.note: No extras of any kind. The offer's standard page, with nothing added on top.

_contract_comment: AI AUTHORING CONTRACTS. What each element is FOR, not just what it renders. The V1 failure this answers: the generator read 'things you want people to know' as 'desirable things' and turned all of them into bragging points -- six cards of prose where the element wants quantities. The questionnaire's structure became the semantics. So a contract states the element's persuasive JOB, what must NOT go in it, and the elements it is confused with -- because the model needs to know where bragging_points stops and numbered_list begins, not merely what each looks like. `routes` names fact-kinds that belong here but have no element of their own: Junior Bay has no feature or benefit element, so those facts land in numbered_list and content_block by contract rather than by the model guessing. Read by describe_vocabulary() into the prompt and by domain/ai_elements.py for deterministic checks -- one source, two consumers.

bragging_points.purpose: Objective evidence that raises perceived value. Numbers a buyer would repeat to a friend.
bragging_points.use_when: A fact is quantified and checkable: units sold, ratings, years in business, a measured quantity, a percentage.
bragging_points.do_not_use_when: The fact is a feature, a benefit, an opinion, a flavour list, or any claim without a number behind it. A thing being GOOD is not a bragging point; a thing being MEASURED is. And a POLICY TERM is never one, however numeric it looks -- a refund window, a warranty length, a returns period or a delivery promise is a commitment the tenant is making, not evidence about the product. Those have their own element (refund_policy), which the page already carries.

fields.value: The stat alone. Short and scannable -- under ~24 characters, and it must carry a figure.
fields.label: What the figure counts, in sentence case.
fields.heading: Optional section heading.

bad.label: Product
bad.why: No figure. An adjective, not evidence.

bad.label: Protein Per Scoop
bad.why: The figure is buried in a sentence. The value is 30g; the rest is the label.

bad.value: Isolated and hydrolyzed for quality absorption
bad.label: Blend Type
bad.why: A feature described at length. Belongs in numbered_list.

bad.label: Flavors Available
bad.why: A spec sheet entry, not proof of anything.

bad.label: Refund window
bad.why: A policy term, not evidence. It is a promise the seller makes, and it belongs in refund_policy -- which is already on the page, so this also says it twice.

confusable_with.numbered_list: Made from stainless steel is a FEATURE -- what it has. Not proof.
confusable_with.content_block: All-day battery life is a BENEFIT -- what you get. Not proof.
confusable_with.faq: Can I cancel? is an objection to answer, not evidence to display.

rules: With exactly one item, set the section tone to contrast so it breaks the page rhythm rather than reading as a lonely card.

numbered_list.purpose: What the product HAS or what the buyer DOES, in order. This is where FEATURES live -- Junior Bay has no separate feature element, and this is it by contract.
numbered_list.use_when: Several facts of the same kind: materials, specifications, included items, or the steps of a process.
numbered_list.do_not_use_when: The fact is quantified proof (bragging_points), a single idea developed at length (content_block), or a question (faq).

fields.items: ONE LINE each, as a plain string -- not an object. Name the feature or step, then say what it is or what happens, in the same sentence.
fields.heading: Optional section heading. It is what separates a feature list from a how-it-works list, so it carries real meaning.

good: Stainless steel construction — double-walled, so it holds temperature for hours.
Third-party tested — every batch, by an independent lab.
Connects over USB-C — one cable for power and picture.

bad.why: An adjective on its own says nothing a buyer can picture.
An OBJECT. Items are plain strings; the renderer prints one line per item, and an object reaches the page as [object Object].

confusable_with.bragging_points: A feature says what it IS. A bragging point says how MUCH or how MANY.
confusable_with.content_block: A list is several parallel facts. A block is one idea explained.

content_block.purpose: One idea, explained in prose. This is where BENEFITS live -- what the buyer GAINS, and why a feature matters to them.
content_block.use_when: A fact needs a sentence or two of context to land: what it means for the buyer, or why it was built that way.
content_block.do_not_use_when: The point is a bare fact (numbered_list), a figure (bragging_points), or an answer to a question someone asked (faq).

fields.heading: What this block is about, in a few words.
fields.body: Two to four sentences. The benefit, and the feature it rests on.

good.heading: Protein without the mixing
good.body: A full serving in a chewable, so it fits a routine rather than interrupting one.

bad.heading: Features
bad.body: Stainless steel. BPA free. Dishwasher safe.
bad.why: A list wearing a paragraph's clothes. Use numbered_list.

confusable_with.numbered_list: A benefit explains why a feature matters. The feature itself is a list item.
confusable_with.quote: A block argues. A quote is one line of that argument, set large.

faq.purpose: Answer the objections that stop a purchase, in the buyer's own words.
faq.use_when: A buyer would plausibly ask it before paying, and the brief answers it.
faq.do_not_use_when: The brief does not answer it. An invented answer to can I cancel is a contractual promise nobody made -- the single most common failure measured (A.7).

fields.question: As a buyer would type it.
fields.answer: Two sentences at most, and only what the brief supports.
fields.heading: Optional section heading.

bad.question: Can I cancel anytime?
bad.answer: Yes, no lock-in and no fees.
bad.why: A cancellation term the brief never gave. Measured invention.

confusable_with.content_block: An FAQ answers a question someone asked. A block makes a point nobody asked for.

headline.purpose: The page's single claim. The one thing a buyer should remember.
headline.use_when: Always. Every page has exactly one.

fields.text: One line. Wrap two or three words in ** ** to mark them.

good.text: **30g of protein.** No shaker, no mess.

confusable_with.subheadline: The headline claims. The subheadline qualifies.

subheadline.purpose: Qualify the headline with the facts that make it credible.
subheadline.use_when: The headline needs supporting specifics to be believed.
subheadline.do_not_use_when: It would repeat the headline in other words.

fields.text: One or two sentences of the concrete facts behind the claim.

good.text: 60 gummies per tub, third-party lab tested, made in the USA.

bad.text: The best protein you can buy.

quote.purpose: One line of the page's own argument, set large to slow the reader down.
quote.use_when: A single sentence carries the whole pitch and deserves emphasis.
quote.do_not_use_when: The line would be attributed to a customer. An attributed quote is a testimonial, and a generated testimonial is a fabricated review (A.7). This element carries no attribution and must never imply one.

fields.text: One sentence, in the brand's voice, unattributed.

good.text: The hardest part of a supplement is remembering to take it.

bad.text: Best protein I have ever had! -- Sarah M.
bad.why: An invented customer. Real ones come from Reviews.

confusable_with.content_block: A quote is one line. A block is the paragraph around it.

page_ribbon.purpose: A thin band of reassurances, scanned rather than read.
page_ribbon.use_when: Three or four short facts already stated elsewhere deserve repeating at a glance.
page_ribbon.do_not_use_when: The facts are not in the brief. A ribbon is the densest place to put a claim nobody made.

fields.headline: Short phrases separated by a middle dot.
fields.body: The line under it, if the ribbon needs one.

good.text: Third-party tested · Made in the USA · Free US shipping

confusable_with.bragging_points: A ribbon repeats; bragging points establish.

seo_title.purpose: What a search result shows. Written for someone who has not seen the page.

fields.label: Under 60 characters. Product, then its most searchable attribute.

good.text: Creatine Gummies - 5g per serving, 60 per tub

confusable_with.headline: The title is for search. The headline is for the page.

hero.purpose: The line under the product's name at the top of the page.

fields.headline: A short phrase. Not a sentence.
fields.subheadline: The line under the headline. Falls back to the product description when absent.

bad.tagline: Our product is a high-quality supplement designed for athletes
bad.why: A paragraph in a phrase's place.

confusable_with.headline: The hero introduces. The headline claims.

author_bio.purpose: Who made this, when that is part of why to trust it.
author_bio.use_when: The brief says who is behind the product and it matters to the buyer.
author_bio.do_not_use_when: The brief does not name a person. Inventing a founder is fabricating a person.

good.heading: Dr Amara Osei, formulator
good.body: Fifteen years in sports nutrition before starting the company.

confusable_with.content_block: A bio is about a person; a block is about the product.
